claim: Compared with SCPs, declarative policies give a simpler way to define a configuration and show end users why their actions failed through customizable error messages.
question: How do declarative policies differ from SCPs for end users?

evidence.quote: Declarative policies provide a simpler way to define the configuration, and provide end users visibility into why their actions failed through customizable error messages.

claim: With declarative policies you do not have to update SCPs for new APIs to protect a configuration; once set, a declarative policy maintains the configuration.
question: Why use a declarative policy instead of only SCPs to protect a configuration?

values.display: you do not have to update your SCPs with new APIs
a declarative policy will maintain the configuration

evidence.quote: With declarative policies, you do not have to update your SCPs with new APIs to protect your configuration objective. Once set, a declarative policy will maintain the configuration.

claim: Where existing SCPs cover a control that declarative policies support, adding that control to a declarative policy is an additional layer of protection.
question: Do declarative policies replace existing SCPs for the same control?

evidence.quote: If you have existing SCPs for a control supported by declarative policies, adding them to a declarative policy will serve as an additional layer of protection to enforce the desired configuration.

claim: Next to SCPs, RCPs and declarative policies, you can keep using AWS Config detective rules to monitor changes and AWS Config proactive rules to prevent non-compliant resources created through CloudFormation.
question: Which AWS Config rule types work alongside organization policies, and what does each do?

evidence.quote: You can continue to leverage AWS Config detective rules for continuously monitoring changes in their environment and AWS Config proactive rules to prevent creation of non-compliant resources through CloudFormation.

claim: Once enforced, a declarative policy prevents non-compliant actions, and its configuration is kept when AWS adds new APIs and features or when resources, principals or accounts are added to the organization.
question: What does a declarative policy do once it is enforced?

evidence.quote: Once enforced, these policies prevent non-compliant actions. The configuration defined in the declarative policy is maintained when AWS introduces new APIs and features or if there are changes to your organization such as addition of resources, principals and accounts.

claim: SCPs set the maximum available permissions for IAM users and IAM roles, while RCPs set the maximum available permissions for resources.
question: What is the difference between an SCP and an RCP?

values.display: maximum available permissions for IAM users and IAM roles

evidence.quote: Service control policies (SCPs) offer central control over the maximum available permissions for IAM users and IAM roles in an organization.
Resource control policies (RCPs) offer central control over the maximum available permissions for resources in an organization.

claim: Backup policies let you centrally manage and apply backup plans to resources across the accounts of an organization.
question: Which organization policy applies backup plans across accounts?

values.display: centrally manage and apply backup plans

evidence.quote: Backup policies allow you to centrally manage and apply backup plans to the AWS resources across an organization's accounts.

claim: Tag policies let you standardize the tags attached to resources in the accounts of an organization.
question: Which organization policy standardizes tags?

values.display: standardize the tags attached to the AWS resources

evidence.quote: Tag policies allow you to standardize the tags attached to the AWS resources in an organization's accounts.

claim: AI services opt-out policies let you control data collection for AWS AI services for all accounts in an organization.
question: Which organization policy controls data collection by AWS AI services?

values.display: control data collection for AWS AI services

evidence.quote: AI services opt-out policies allow you to control data collection for AWS AI services for all the accounts in an organization.

claim: To use an AWS service integrated with AWS Organizations, you go to that service in the console and enable the integration there.
question: Where do you enable an AWS service integration with Organizations?

values.display: navigate in the AWS Management Console to that service

evidence.quote: To get started using an AWS service integrated with AWS Organization, navigate in the AWS Management Console to that service and enable the integration.
